title: Ho-Lee, Time-Dependent Drift and Volatility
august: Ho-Lee numerical - plug values; time-dependent drift and vol - theory question.

maps.tested: One sheet writes 'calculations are super important here': this is one of the few places where the quantitative work is the whole question. Two-step binomial node construction is the dominant format.
maps.specifics: Highly specific recalls: 'calculate interest rate after 2 months in the top node in Ho-Lee model'; 'Ho Lee and time-dependent volatility models: calculate value of rate in upper nodes'; 'Ho Lee Model & Model 3, 2-step plug and play calculation'; 'no-arbitrage model (Node 2 delta r)'; '2 on IR term structure (Ho Lee)'. Node formula: r0 + sum of lambda x dt +/- m x sigma x sqrt(dt). Sibling swap risk against Vasicek and Model 1/2.

vardeezReading: MR-14: Very Important. "Vasicek Model Calc can come; Ho-Lee Model; Calc of Expected Rate in 7 years (LO 14.g). Note: Calculations are super imp here." MR-15: Very Important. "CIR model; Concept of Terminal Distributions; Model 3; Lognormal Model (Deterministic Drift). Understand Interpretation."

selectors.name: Ho-Lee top node after two months
selectors.what: Interest rate after 2 months in the top node of a monthly Ho-Lee tree (dt = 1/12): r0 + (lambda1 + lambda2) x dt + 2 x sigma x sqrt(dt), the change from today being the drift sum plus two up moves.
selectors.theory: Why date-2 nodes carry the sum of the two period drifts, why the volatility perturbation scales with sqrt(dt) and the drift with dt, why the top node needs two up moves, and why the tree recombines (constant sigma).

selectors.name: Rate in upper nodes, Ho-Lee or Model 3
selectors.what: Value of the short rate in the upper nodes of a Ho-Lee tree (constant sigma) or of a time-dependent-volatility tree (Model 3, dr = lambda(t) dt + sigma(t) dw with sigma(t) = sigma x e^(-alpha t)), built step by step from the stated drifts and volatilities.
selectors.theory: How the drift and the volatility enter each node, what changes when volatility is time-dependent (the branches shrink as sigma(t) decays; reusing the initial sigma is Ho-Lee), and that the volatility term structure stays flat.

selectors.name: Ho-Lee and Model 3 two-step plug and play
selectors.what: Two-step calculation with given inputs: Ho-Lee upper node r0 + (lambda1 + lambda2) dt + 2 sigma sqrt(dt); Model 3 upper node r0 + (lambda1 + lambda2) dt + [sigma(t1) + sigma(t2)] sqrt(dt); and the two-step standard deviation sqrt(dt) x sqrt(sigma(t1)^2 + sigma(t2)^2).
selectors.theory: How the standard deviation of the terminal distribution behaves under Model 3 (it rises quickly with the horizon at first, then more slowly), why standard deviations add in quadrature and not linearly, and when Model 3 gives the same terminal distribution as Vasicek.

selectors.name: No-arbitrage model, node-2 change and drift
selectors.what: Change in the short rate at node 2 of a Ho-Lee tree, (lambda1 + lambda2) dt + 2 sigma sqrt(dt) for the top node, and the drift and volatility read back from given nodes: lambda1 = [(ru + rd)/2 - r0] / dt and sigma = (ru - rd) / (2 sqrt(dt)). Includes the uses of arbitrage-free models and the fitting issue.
selectors.theory: Ho-Lee is calibrated so the tree reproduces the market rates it is given (lambda1 from the two-month rate, lambda2 from the three-month rate, and so on), hence arbitrage-free; its uses (quoting illiquid securities, valuing and hedging derivatives); and the cautions on fitting (a bad model is not rescued by calibration, prices are not always fair, a drift that jumps year to year is suspect, relative value needs equilibrium models).

selectors.name: Two questions on the Ho-Lee short-rate tree
selectors.what: The 'two on interest rate term structure (Ho-Lee)' pair: node values on the monthly tree (date-1 nodes r0 + lambda1 dt +/- sigma sqrt(dt); date-2 nodes r0 + (lambda1 + lambda2) dt + {2, 0, -2} sigma sqrt(dt)) and a reverse-solve for the drift or the volatility from given nodes.
selectors.theory: Calibration logic of the tree: the free drift parameters are fitted to the market curve, volatility is constant, each branch has probability 1/2, and the date-2 range is 4 sigma sqrt(dt).

selectors.name: Sibling swap: Vasicek, Models 1 and 2
selectors.what: A question that sets Ho-Lee or time-dependent volatility beside its siblings: Model 1 (dr = sigma dw, no drift), Model 2 (dr = lambda dt + sigma dw, constant drift) and Vasicek (mean reversion), on drift, mean reversion, flat or humped volatility term structure, parallel shifts and negative rates.

selectors.name: August plain forms: Ho-Lee, drift, volatility
selectors.what: The two plain forms recalled from August 2026: a Ho-Lee numerical with plug-in values, and a theory question on time-dependent drift and time-dependent volatility.
selectors.theory: A time-dependent drift fits the market's bond or swap rates and a time-dependent volatility fits option (caplet) prices; neither adds mean reversion, so both remain normal parallel-shift models with a flat volatility term structure and a possibility of negative rates.

notSelected: MR-14 c (methods for negative short rates: topic D1), MR-15 c (efficacy of time-dependent volatility models beyond the S7 theory), and MR-14 g and h (Vasicek calculations and effectiveness: topic A25) carry no selector here; MR-14 a and b (Model 1 and Model 2 construction) and MR-14 f (Vasicek tree) are covered only as the sibling comparison in S6, and the CIR and lognormal readings MR-15 d, e and f belong to topic D1.
